body:
Found while reviewing #476. **Blocking #476.** Fix the workflow-facing secrets grammar before it becomes a public habit. This supersedes item 4 of #477.

## 1. `WithYields` must not carry down the context
Outputs belong to a single producer, but `WithYields` stores them on the context, so every later operation inherits them. Probe (local, against `7a595bf`):
```go
ctx = gimbal.WithYields(ctx, "", "DATABASE_URL")
gimbal.RunCommand(ctx, "produce", "", "sh", "-c", `printf 'DATABASE_URL=x\n' > "$ENV_FILE"`) // ok
gimbal.RunCommand(ctx, "unrelated", "", "true") // fails: producer output file unavailable; scope fails
```
Requirements accumulating through the context is correct, because it mirrors scope visibility. Outputs carrying down is not. Either make outputs a property of the operation itself, or at least add a lint rule that `WithYields` may only appear inline as the context argument of `Service`/`RunCommand`/`Check`.

## 2. Make requiring and producing look alike
Today:
```go
gimbal.WithYields(ctx, "", "WEB_URL")
gimbal.WithRequirements(ctx, gimbal.StoreRequirement{Names: []string{"DATABASE_URL"}})
```
`WithRequirements` already accumulates, so `WithRequirements(ctx, store, names...)` covers multiple stores through repeated calls. Then drop the exported `StoreRequirement`/`Requirements` aliases from package `gimbal` and simplify GIMBAL111, which currently guesses that `Names` is the second positional field. Replace the magic `""` with a named default-store constant.

## 3. `SecretsBackend.Publish` takes a named write (endorsed by Tyler)
`Publish(context.Context, Scope, string, map[string]string)` has two unnamed strings, so the docs don't say which is the store. Use named types, with the same structure as `StoreRequirement`:
```go
type NamedValue struct{ Name, Value string }
type StoreWrite struct {
	Store  string
	Values []NamedValue
}
Publish(ctx context.Context, scope Scope, write StoreWrite) error
```
Duplicate names in a write fail. Name the other interface parameters too (`AcquireEnvironment(ctx, owner, name)`, etc.).

## 4. Show declarations in the source graph
The contract says declarations stay "available to the source-derived workflow graph". `internal/generate` doesn't read `WithYields` or `WithRequirements`, so the `service-check` graph shows the services but not what they publish or what consumers need. Add outputs (store + names) to `Service`/`Command` operations, and requirements to consuming operations.
title: Fix the workflow secrets grammar: scoped yields, symmetric requirements, named StoreWrite, graph visibility
